options: The historical standard deviation of the stock's past returns
The volatility that will actually occur over the option's life, known with certainty
The value of sigma that, when plugged into Black-Scholes along with the observable inputs, reproduces the option's actual market price
A fixed constant set by the exchange for every option
questions.explain: Implied volatility is found by running Black-Scholes backward: given the market price and the observable inputs, solve for the sigma that makes the formula match that price.

questions.q: Why can't implied volatility be solved for algebraically?
options: Because volatility is always zero in theory
Because sigma appears inside the cumulative normal distribution terms N(d1) and N(d2) in a way that cannot be isolated on one side of the equation
Because Black-Scholes does not use volatility as an input
Because implied volatility is a government-regulated number
questions.explain: The nonlinear way sigma enters d1, d2, and the normal CDF makes direct algebraic inversion impossible, so implied volatility must be found numerically via root-finding methods.

questions.q: What does a volatility skew in equity index options typically show?
options: Implied volatility is identical across every strike, exactly as Black-Scholes predicts
Implied volatility is higher for low (downside) strikes than for high strikes, often attributed to demand for crash/downside protection
Implied volatility is higher only for at-the-money options
Implied volatility is unrelated to strike price in any market
questions.explain: The typical equity index skew shows higher implied volatility at low strikes, consistent with investors bidding up the price of downside puts used to hedge against market crashes.

questions.q: What does the existence of the volatility smile/skew reveal about the Black-Scholes model's assumptions?
options: Nothing — the smile is unrelated to any model assumption
It directly shows that the constant-volatility assumption behind Black-Scholes does not hold in real markets
It proves that stock returns are perfectly lognormal
It proves that interest rates are the only input that varies in real markets
questions.explain: If volatility were truly constant across strikes as Black-Scholes assumes, every strike would produce the same implied volatility. The observed variation is direct evidence the assumption fails empirically.

options: A single number representing the market's average volatility across all options
Implied volatility plotted as a function of both strike price and time to expiration, forming a full 3D map
The historical volatility chart of a single stock over the last year
A regulatory report filed daily by every options exchange
questions.explain: The volatility surface combines the strike dimension (smile/skew) and the expiration dimension (term structure) into a single map of implied volatility that trading desks monitor as its own source of information.
